newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - New issue frenzy continues.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - New issue frenzy continues.

text.p: The new issue frenzy continued on Wednesday with another $2.5 billion in straight corporate debt hitting the market, bringing this week's total so far to over $5.0 billion, dealers said.
"The market was definitely being driven by new issues," said one high-grade trader. "It also brought out some secondary paper, which is being picked up by retail."
Falling U.S. interest rates have been driving the recent surge in supply. The 10-year U.S. Treasury note dropped to a yield of 6.25 percent Wednesday from 6.50 percent less than two weeks ago.
The benchmark 30-year bond fell to a level of 6.56 percent from 6.78 percent during the same period.

Among Wednesday's issuers was Federated Department Stores which issued $250 million in 30-year bonds at 57 basis points and $300 million in 20-year debentures at 90 basis points. Goldman Sachs & Co was lead manager on the deal.
Another issuer, PNC Bank Corp, also sold $350 million in 10-year notes at 67 basis points over via Smith Barney.
Also, Travelers Group unit, Smith Barney sold $250 million in five-year notes at 48 basis points for themselves.
Private Export Funding with a $100 million 10-year deal at 25 basis points over Treasuries via Citicorp Securities.
Williams Cos unit, Texas Gas Transmission also set $100 million in 30-year bonds at 75 basis points over.
Meanwhile, the busy pace in the primary sector spilled into the secondary trading arena with players seeing good two-way flow and spreads seen a touch tighter.
After news of Moody's Investors Service upgrade to Citicorp and BankAmerica Corp credit ratings the banks' paper tightened two basis points, bank and finance traders said.
Moody's raised both banks' senior debt ratings to Aa3 from A1.
Turning to the high-yield sector, Nebco Evans Holding Co sold $55 million (proceeds) in 10-year notes with a five-year zero coupon at a 12.375 percent.
Also, Nebco unit, Ameriserve Food Distribution, sold $500 million in 10-year 144A debt to yield 10-1/4 percent, sources said.
Players said Ameriserve Food's 10-1/8 percent bonds, which priced at par, traded up to a 101-3/8 bid by the close.
In the high-yield secondary trading arena, Grand Union 12 percent debt fell 1-3/4 points to trade at 68-1/4 bid, 69 offer, players said.
"Grand Union bonds had a volatile day of trading...they were all over the place," said one high-yield trader.
Players said yesteday the bonds closed at a 70 bid.
Among other surpermarket issues, Pathmark Stores zeros were quoted 68-3/4 bid, 69-1/2 offer, players said.
Elsewhere, Payless Cashways 9.125 percent paper continued weaker, trading off another 3/4 to 23-3/4 bid, 24-1/2 offer, traders said.

The Kansas City-based specialty retailer's bonds have continued under pressure after disappointing second quarter operating results, a debt restructuring announcement, and downgrades to the firm's credit ratings.
